title: The Ablative Absolute
subtitle: Caesare duce — with Caesar as leader. Latin's compact alternative to subordinate clauses.
objectives: Translate ablative absolutes with 'with X being', 'when X was', 'since X is', etc.
Understand that the ablative absolute is grammatically independent of the main sentence.

sections.heading: The ablative absolute
sections.body:
The ablative absolute is a noun (or pronoun) + participle (or adjective/noun), both in the ablative, grammatically independent of the main sentence.

Caesare duce — with Caesar (as) leader, when Caesar was leader
Caesare interfectō — Caesar having been killed, when Caesar was killed
hīs dictīs — these things having been said

Caesar writes: hīs rēbus cognitīs, Caesar exercitum dūxit. — These things having been learned, Caesar led the army.
Cicero writes: Caesare cōnsule. — When Caesar was consul.

items.answer: The city having been captured / when the city was captured.
The enemies having been conquered / with the enemies conquered.

words.gloss: The city having been captured, the soldiers departed.
